source.extractedText: Let A={1,2,3,4,...,45} and R be the relation defined as “square is of a number” on A. Write R as a subset of A×A. Also, find the domain and range of R.
source.fidelityCaution: The original extraction corrupts A×A notation; inspect PDF page image and confirm orientation of 'square is of a number' before source certification.

interpretation: (x,y) belongs to R when x is the square of y; x,y in A
stepsEnglish: A relation on A consists of ordered pairs (x,y) with both entries in A.
Read 'x is the square of y' as x = y². This orientation must be checked against the printed page.
Since x ≤ 45, y² ≤ 45; the positive integers y = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 qualify, but 7² = 49 is too large.
The domain is the set of first coordinates: {1,4,9,16,25,36}.
The range is the set of second coordinates: {1,2,3,4,5,6}.
Check each pair by squaring its second coordinate and confirming the first coordinate is in A.
